title: Garlic Tarragon Shrimp Skewers
seoTitle: Garlic Tarragon Shrimp Skewers | Firehall BBQ
shortDescription: Shrimp skewer night—fast grocery-store shellfish on the hall grill
subtitle: Charred jumbo shrimp, shallot-tarragon butter, and lemon for ten
description: Large jumbo shrimp thread onto skewers, grill until charred and 140°F, and finish with sizzling garlic-lemon butter and fresh parsley.

steps.title: Prep shrimp
steps.instruction: Pat shrimp completely dry with paper towels. Season with salt and pepper. Plan about 15 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Use micro arugula as listed — measure each before heat goes on. Target 145°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Build garlic butter
steps.instruction: Melt butter with garlic and shallots over low heat 3 minutes. Off heat, add tarragon, wine, lemon juice and zest. Keep warm, not boiling.

steps.title: Heat grill hot
steps.instruction: Preheat grill to high, 450°F. Oil grates generously—wet shrimp stick. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 145°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Skewer shrimp
steps.instruction: Thread 3–4 shrimp per skewer with small gaps. Brush lightly with grapeseed oil. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 145°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Grill shrimp
steps.instruction: Grill skewers 2 minutes per side until pink and 140°F internal. Do not overcook. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 145°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Brief rest
steps.instruction: Rest skewers 2 minutes off heat. Transfer to hotel pans. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Butter at service
steps.instruction: Spoon warm garlic butter over shrimp at the line. Scatter parsley. Hold covered at 140°F up to 10 minutes max. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 145°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Platter for ten
steps.instruction: Serve 4 shrimp per firefighter with bread for soaking butter. Call it fast—shrimp waits poorly. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 145°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

proTips: Dry shrimp are non-negotiable—moisture prevents the sear.
Two minutes per side max; rubber shrimp mean the grill was too slow or too long.
Garlic butter at the line keeps shrimp from steaming under foil.
tonightSpread: Garlic butter shrimp skewers with crusty bread.
Simple arugula salad with lemon vinaigrette.
leftovers: Chop shrimp into pasta with extra butter.
Flake into breakfast hash with potatoes.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Shrimp cooks faster than any protein on the line and is in every grocery freezer case. Brief hold at 140°F max—works for a quick hall meal between calls.
mealPrepNotes: Pat shrimp completely dry. Grill high 450°F—2 minutes per side max. Hold covered at 140°F up to 10 minutes only. Garlic butter at service, not during hold.
